derate_vs_derailment: DE-RATE by the letter (estimates up, multiple down) but the test is NOT DIAGNOSTIC FOR CYCLICALS. In subscription software stable forward estimates evidence durability because the revenue is contracted; in semi-cap, guidance is a LAGGING indicator — the cycle turns after the last strong guide, because the order book converts on a 2-4 quarter delay and cancellations surface only once the customer's own capex plan is cut. Applying the HUBS/CTSH/SAP winner pattern here is a category error. LESSON TO ENCODE: weight estimate stability by revenue contractedness.

edge_explainer: Nova is a genuinely good business beating and raising into a 35% collapse, which is exactly the setup the house's de-rate-vs-derailment test is built to buy — and that is the trap. The test measures whether estimates are holding, but in semiconductor capital equipment estimates are the last thing to break: the order book converts on a two-to-four-quarter delay, so management is still guiding up while the customer's capex plan is already being cut. What the tape shows is a capex break transmitting through the equipment layer first — the whole WFE complex is down 13-36% since mid-June while the S&P is down 1% and Nvidia 5%. Nova is the leading edge of the exact break the house has frozen at 45%, and after the de-rate it still trades near 40x forward earnings, which is not a broken-cycle price. Add a 7-22pp unexplained underperformance versus its own US peers, a low that is three sessions old, and a print in three days, and there is no version of this entry that is anything but catching the knife early.
